disruption of BCAA c-atabolism in mice leads to elevated plasma BCAAS, decreased fat mass, increased energy expenditure, improved glucose tolerance, and resistance to diet-induced obesity.

the regulation of energy expenditure by peripheral branched-chain amino acids.
the role of bran-ched-chain amino acid metabolism in regulating energy homeostasis and insulin sensitivity.
the role of bran-ched-chain amino acids and branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase as regulators of energy balance and metabolism in mice.
